assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its conversion into incretin-based drugs for type 2 diabetes and obesity is a discovery chain of exceptional importance: the incretin concept, identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, its insulinotropic and satiety actions, and the resulting therapies that now change outcomes in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular risk. As a neurologist I also note central appetite and emerging neuroprotective effects, but the case stands on endocrinology and clinical impact alone.
assessment.attribution: The decisive scientific contributions are best credited to Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptides, GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, translation to therapy) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide). Knudsen drove the drug-development step at an industrial laboratory, and Habener, who is not in the supplied credit list, also made major contributions; a three-person physiology-focused configuration is defensible but leaves real credit tension.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is overwhelming and independent: multiple approved agents, large randomised outcome trials and global use. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue; the main risk is the attribution dispute, not maturity.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among Mojsov, Habener, Holst and Drucker is contested and I cannot independently adjudicate it.
The role of the medicinal-chemistry and drug-development contribution (Knudsen) versus the physiological discovery may favour a split of the award.
My recollection of the detailed discovery chronology is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new class of organelle-to-nucleus signalling, with IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and later PERK/ATF6 arms. It underlies understanding of secretory-cell physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration, and cancer, and has clear conceptual originality and lasting impact on cell biology and disease mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily identified the IRE1 signalling pathway and the transcriptional program, with Walter also defining the mechanism of splicing and kinase/RNase activation. The two-person configuration is clean and well supported by the credited names; David Ron and others, if relevant, are not in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed across yeast and mammals over more than two decades, with stable interpretation. Clinical translation is still partial, but the basic discovery is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Translational impact is still emerging, as the pharmacology of UPR modulators is not yet established in approved drugs.
Contributions of other investigators (for example in the PERK arm) are outside the supplied credit list and may be argued as necessary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells created a new modality of living drugs, with curative responses in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas and now expanding into myeloma and autoimmune disease. This is a major and original clinical advance with strong patient impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed the early conceptual and co-stimulatory CAR designs; June led the clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB signalling. Rosenberg's adoptive-cell-therapy work and the earliest chimeric-receptor concept by others (Eshhar, not in the list) complicate credit. A two-person award is plausible but leaves an unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long-term remissions support maturity, though long-term toxicity and durability data continue to accrue. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Eshhar is not in the supplied credited names, so the earliest CAR concept is not representable.
Allocation among June, Sadelain and Rosenberg is genuinely uncertain.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a way to control defined cell populations with millisecond precision, transforming the causal study of circuits and behaviour and enabling early therapeutic applications such as vision restoration. Its impact on basic research is very broad, in a field close to my own.
assessment.attribution: The discovery is a compound one: channelrhodopsin identification and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), neuronal expression and application (Boyden, Deisseroth), and the earlier genetically targeted photostimulation concept (Miesenböck). Six names cannot fit; a configuration of Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel prioritises the tool's conceptual and biophysical foundations plus its neuroscience deployment, but sacrifices Bamberg and Boyden.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and standard across laboratories for over a decade. Clinical translation remains early, but the tool-based impact is mature.
uncertainties: Credit split among six credible contributors is highly contested and a three-person limit forces an exclusion that may not be fair.
Whether a methods tool fits the Physiology or Medicine prize at this point is a judgement call, not a factual question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense therapy for spinal muscular atrophy (nusinersen) turned a fatal infant motor neuron disease into a treatable one, and proved that rational RNA-targeted drugs can act in the CNS. The mechanistic insight on SMN2 exon 7 splicing and the clinical result are both strong; this speaks directly to neurological practice.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing regulatory mechanism and the antisense strategy at the academic stage, and Bennett led the optimisation and development of the oligonucleotide chemistry and drug. Adrian Krainer and Bennett form a coherent pair; contributions from the SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) and from other antisense chemistry pioneers are outside the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of real-world data. Independent confirmation exists through other SMA therapies, though the field is young relative to older candidates, so recognition would be slightly early.
uncertainties: The prize may reasonably be thought premature relative to older foundational antisense work.
Relative contribution of antisense chemistry pioneers beyond the credited names is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as a central regulator of growth, nutrient sensing and metabolism is a foundational advance with far-reaching implications for cancer, ageing, immunity and metabolic disease. It is original and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically and defined its role in growth control; Schreiber's chemical-biology work on FKBP12-rapamycin provided the pharmacological handle. Sabatini and others elucidated mTOR complexes in mammals, and Heitman and Hall's yeast work is closely related. A Hall-led configuration is plausible, but the second laureate is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed over three decades; clinical use of rapalogs is established, though the therapeutic breakthrough is more modest than the conceptual one.
uncertainties: The best second or third laureate is unclear and Sabatini carries a reputational question I do not assess here.
Relative contributions of the yeast genetics and the chemical-biology work are not fully settled in my view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation transformed treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor, and opened neuromodulation as a therapeutic field for dystonia, OCD and other circuits. As a neurologist who treats these patients, I regard the clinical benefit as substantial and durable.
assessment.attribution: Benabid's introduction of high-frequency thalamic and subthalamic stimulation is the central contribution on the supplied credit list. The subthalamic target rationale built on work by DeLong and others, who are not in the supplied names, so a single-laureate award would be incomplete in the larger historical picture.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of clinical use and randomised trials give strong confirmation. Recognition is mature and the field has had earlier Lasker recognition.
uncertainties: Contributions of DeLong, Bergman and Limousin are not represented in the credited names.
The mechanism of action of DBS remains incompletely understood.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of tau and alpha-synuclein as the molecular components of the characteristic filamentous inclusions in Alzheimer's disease, Lewy body disease and related disorders reframed neurodegeneration as a protein-aggregation problem. It underpins biomarker assays, seed-amplification tests, structural classification of tauopathies and many current drug programmes.
assessment.attribution: Spillantini and Goedert jointly identified alpha-synuclein in Lewy bodies and tau in paired helical filaments with biochemical and genetic follow-up. The pair is a coherent configuration; related discoveries by Lee and Trojanowski, and Kosik and Wischik, are not in the credited names and may be argued.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and extended by cryo-EM structures and diagnostic applications. Disease-modifying therapies are still lacking, so clinical vindication is incomplete but the molecular discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Absence of an effective disease-modifying therapy limits the translational argument.
Other groups with competing priority claims are outside the supplied credit list.
I have a research overlap with Parkinson's disease and should not treat that as an advantage.
